newsitem.title: UK: POLICE QUESTION GOALKEEPER BOSNICH OVER NAZI SALUTE.
newsitem.headline: POLICE QUESTION GOALKEEPER BOSNICH OVER NAZI SALUTE.

text.p: Australian goalkeeper Mark Bosnich was questioned by police on Saturday after giving a Nazi salute during a match between his British team Aston Villa and London club Tottenham Hotspur, which has a large Jewish following.
Bosnich, made the salute after the crowd taunted him about a clash two seasons ago with Tottenham's former striker, Jurgen Klinsmann, that saw the German stretchered unconscious off the pitch.
Bosnich, who is of Croatian descent, was booked for "ungentlemanly conduct" after the salute. Tottenham beat Aston Villa 1-0.
Police said they summoned Bosnich for questioning following public complaints, but that he was not arrested or charged. "The police investigation is continuing," said a police spokesman.
Bosnich later apologised on British radio.
"For me it was a real joke, but it's been taken so much out of proportion and I'm so, so sorry," he said.
"I know the Spurs fans have lost people in the war, but I also lost people in the war. I believe in free speech."
